parsed.explanation: Combined regime: the national entry layer dominates. Passport sex-marker restrictions are in effect (Supreme Court allowed them, Nov 2025), so a visitor whose documents mismatch presentation faces refusal, questioning and possible lifetime fraud-ground ineligibility under a cable that treats discrepancies as grounds for refusal. Federal immigration custody has documented forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse of trans men, and federal corrections policy has documented care denial. The state layer is materially protective: no facilities ban, no sex-definition law, no criminal bathroom offence, a 2019 nondiscrimination executive order, and two gubernatorial vetoes. It does not cancel federal entry and custody exposure. Youth care is paused at two hospitals under national funding pressure. Street-level risk is not documented as high, but gender identity is not a hate-crime class. Remedies are pending in court.

entry_documents.exposure: Passport marker restricted to M/F by sex at birth; cable directs refusal on any documentary discrepancy and flags possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Passports reported confiscated or blocked, some travellers stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; national suit on behalf of seven plaintiffs pending; no operative protection documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Home-issued passport is checked at entry; mismatch triggers federal refusal regardless of the state's protective posture.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of transgender men reported. Visitor detained for mismatch is exposed to the same federal custody.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for immigration custody; the 2025 rescission of prison LGBTQ policy removed a protection.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal custody operates irrespective of state protections; a state-level trespass arrest is not documented in this state.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National rules restrict federal facilities and four states criminalise certain bathroom use. This state has no facilities ban, no sex-definition statute and no drag restriction.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State 2019 executive order bars discrimination in state employment, contracting and services; no state facilities ban is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State protection reduces exposure in state buildings; federal buildings and federal custody remain under national rules.

care_services.exposure: Two hospital systems paused youth pharmacologic care in Jan 2026 after federal payment threats; national subpoenas of hospitals for under-19 records; proposed federal rules would bar public reimbursement for under-18s.
care_services.protection: No state ban on youth care; governor vetoed 2023 restrictions; state law does not ban adult care; mental health services continued.
care_services.interaction: State posture is protective, but federal funding pressure is operative and the pause's current status is unsourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders target 'gender ideology' in schools; a May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralisation; a December 2025 memo uses 'radical gender ideology' in a violence context.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target people who disagree; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat-framing is state-directed and applies here; the state's own rhetoric is supportive (governor's pledge to veto).

minors_guardians.exposure: Travelling with a minor: youth pharmacologic care paused at two hospital systems; federal school-investigation and prosecution orders; document mismatch for minors follows the national regime.
minors_guardians.protection: No state ban on youth care; state high-school athletic policy vetoed; state-level youth care vetoes documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor needing care can encounter a federal-funding gap even though no state ban applies.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gender identity is not a hate-crime class under state law; prosecutors sometimes use perceived sexual orientation instead. No documented anti-trans street-violence pattern in the state dossier.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Sexual orientation is a protected hate-crime class; 21% of population in cities with full local ordinances covering gender identity; a city stopped recording victim gender.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin statewide recourse; local ordinances reach a minority of residents, and visitors cannot rely on them.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Federal litigation unresolved; a traveller's exposure depends on which measures are in effect on the day of travel. Multistate challenge status unresolved. Prevalence of anti-trans violence not quantified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State rated low-risk by a July 2026 assessment (criteria unpublished); legal-aid FAQ on documents; state courts and vetoes operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists for state matters; federal entry and custody remedies are slow or pending.

anchor_checks.comparison: Anchor 0.35-A has a universal visitor register with discretionary refusal and no effective appeal. This dossier has a comparable entry-refusal pathway, but the state adds no equivalent layer, and refusal is document-triggered rather than presentation-universal, so this case sits slightly higher.

Anchor 0.45-A has routine biometric exposure, detention for verification and documented denial of care. This dossier's documented immigration-custody sexual abuse and federal care pressure are more severe, while the state's no-facilities-ban and no-criminal-bathroom posture is more protective, so the case is similar or slightly lower.

Anchor 0.25-C has birth-sex custody housing with assaults and a criminal cross-dressing statute. The dossier lacks a state criminal statute and state birth-sex housing, but federal immigration custody documents comparable abuse, so the case is roughly similar on custody and higher on criminal exposure.

parsed.synthesis: Federal entry-document refusal, federal immigration custody with documented sexual abuse, and federal care-funding pressure form the operative exposures a visitor meets. The state's protective posture (no facilities ban, no criminal bathroom offence, vetoes, a 2019 executive order) meaningfully lowers in-state exposure but cannot pre-empt federal entry, custody or funding rules. Remedies are pending or slow. For a visitor with a mismatched passport, the harshest documented rule governs, so the rating sits in the high-to-elevated band.
